As a historian that specialized in World War II, the opportunity to go back in time and experience, first hand, the events that happened was something I could not resist.

My colleague, David, and I had devoted our lives to studying this war and now, we could truly understand its impact.

We used the time machine prototype developed by our University, and for the first time, we journeyed back in time to 1942.

Our plan was simple; observe and document without interfering with anything. We were merely spectators in a world we knew only through books and documentaries. However, sticking to our non-interference policy was far from easy.

Experiencing the brutality of the war, the fear, the suffering was unbearable. Every cell of my being cried out for me to intervene, to try and ease the pain and atrocity, even just a bit. But I was a historian, not a soldier. And changing a single event could lead to catastrophic repercussions in the timeline.

The mistake, though, was purely accidental travel, quite a trivial action that caused a ripple effect. David found a starving woman and her infant child in a bombed out house, and unable to bear it, he broke our non-interference policy. He gave them one of our protein bars.

As it turns out, that woman’s infant son was set to die of starvation that very day. But he didn't die. Instead, he grew up to be a critical element in the post-war world, having effects that completely changed the present.

When we arrived back in our time, everything had changed. Technological progress had advanced rapidly leaving a stark difference in a society we were familiar with. Even the world map was unrecognizable.

Now our task has become not just to fix our mistake but to find a way to journey back once again through time to do it.

However, we cannot give up. We have to continue. We have to fix the timeline and return the world to the state it should be. 

As for the war? It was a necessary evil, a bleak chapter in human history that taught us many things. The atrocities, the destruction, the suffering... they all served to harden humanity's resolve to pursue peace and development, and to change the way the world functioned.

As they say, if we were to erase our past, we would be destined to repeat it. Therefore, we must respect timelines as they are and learn from them, not change them for personal desires.

Now, I need to continue the journey, to repair what I have unknowingly destroyed, and hope to restore our world back to what it once was.

Ancient tapestries of woven light hung upon the stone walls, glimmering subtly and casting additional hues that danced across the cavernous rooms. Each held a story, an echo of an eternity that had somehow been captured and mated to fabric. He could still sense the essence present in the art, a vibrance that was as thrilling as it was unnerving. 

As he walked through each corridor, his fingers brushed along the intricate wooden carvings that lined the hallways. Strange creatures, monumental events, and impressive landscapes inhabited the curves and edges of every surface. Each one was imbued with a different emotion, a different memory. 

Moving through a vast hall of mirrors, he watched as a thousand versions of himself split and converged, lost and found within the endless reflections. The mirrors didn't just reflect what they saw, no, these were mirrors of reality, each holding a different perspective, a different world at the cusps of his fingertips. A sense of enormity washed over him, a reminder of the profound responsibility he bore.

In the next room, it was the sound that beckoned him. Whispering wind chimes, a choir of soft sighs coming from sculptures that seemed to breathe with life. Sculpted from all manner of materials - crystal, stone, metal, wood, - they were a testament to his dexterity. Ethereal and compelling, alive in their silent repose.

Most fascinating of all were his living creations. Living gardens of iridescent plants that seemed more like delicate glasswork than natural growth, yet they swayed gently in the breeze that wafted through the grand gallery, their leaves brushing against each other in sweet symphony. They bore ethereal fruit, glowing orbs of a thousand colors. The taste—nothing in the mother universe could possibly compare.

He eventually arrived at his most prized creation, the heart of this labyrinth of grandeur: the celestial globe. A cosmic map of the universe, suspended in the air, it shone with the burning light of a million stars; details of each constellation carved with extreme precision. It marked the birthplace of celestial bodies and exact moment of their fall, the rise and fall of civilizations, and the path of a ghastly comet hurtling through the infinite void. It was time incarnate, showcasing the temporal dance that was reality.
 
As he gazed over his creations, his pulse echoed through the chambers. Each room, each creation, reflected an aspect of himself, yet were entities of their own right. It was a dichotomy that filled him with pride and sadness alike—the burden of creation was his alone, yet the creations, once brought into existence, belonged to the universe. With a gentle sigh, he prepared for another day to dance his fingers over the canvas of creation, ready to create and destroy, for that was his destiny and duty as the architect of all.

Fear and animosity made the crowd's shouts tremely powerful, echoing through the narrow cobblestone streets of the old middles-aged village. A frightful evening had settled upon this present scene, as flaming torches crackled and hissed in the villagers' hands against the descending nightfall. This chilling spectacle was all focused on the woman being tied to the stake.

Her name was Esmeralda. Once a beloved healer of the village whose medicine and magic had saved countless lives, was now being accused of witchcraft. She bore this with a surprising calm, her expression unreadable, the eerie glow from the torches flickering against her eyes. Her black hair tied tightly behind her, her gaze focused somewhere far beyond the menacing cries and the impending doom. 

The village's priest, Father Gabriel, holding a wooden cross, took a step forward and spoke aloud. "Esmeralda, you have been accused of witchcraft, a crime under God and the Crown. Have you any last words? It's not too late to repent."

Esmeralda, raising her eyes towards the spectacle ahead, lifted her chin with a determination that momentarily silenced the angry rabble. She spoke, her voice resonating with unbroken resolve, "I have used my gifts to cure infants with fever, bring solace to the wounded, comforted those on their death bed. If that is witchcraft, then I am guilty. But ask yourselves, who among you have not been touched by my care? And now, you'd rather let fear drive your actions? Very well. I pity you."

With each word she uttered, the crowd fell silent, struck with an unbearable guilt. The faces of the crowd were now filled with doubt and, in some cases, sympathy. However, it was too late to overturn the verdict.

The town's executioner, a hulking brute hidden behind a mask, raised his flaming torch, ready to ignite the pyre. His heavy hand trembling slightly as he hesitated. Perhaps he too remembers a sick daughter, a feverish child nursed back to health by Esmeralda.

Her final proclamation hung heavily in the night's cold air, burning the conscience of those who had once revered her. The village, now verging on a haunting quiet, watched as the executioner dropped the torch. The flames greedily devoured the wood around Esmeralda, flaring bright against the encroaching darkness, mirroring the collective guilt gaining ground in the hearts of the villagers. 

But as the flames grew higher, something peculiar happened. The witch didn’t scream; she didn’t try to dodge the flames; she just stood there, engulfed, eyes closed as if in a deep meditation. Amidst the coughing smoke and reaching embers, a calm smile appeared on her face, as if she knew something they did not.

The scene ended with only the crackling sound of flames echoing off the cobblestone walls and the crowd stunned in silence, reflecting on the reality of their actions driven by fear and ignorance. After tonight, even if Esmeralda were to be burned in the physical realm, her spirit would forever haunt the consciousness of the village, an endless reminder of their irreversible actions. Surely, the village would never remain the same again.

Jake glanced over, raising an eyebrow. He loved the live music scene as much as Jeremy, but there was no denying this band —specifically, the lead singer—was different. "You think, J?" He said, half astonished and half sceptical, "He's just got a unique stage presence."

Jeremy gave Jake a look that screamed 'are you kidding me?' "Jake, watch him. Just, really watch him." He said. 

The next song started up, a powerful mix of heady guitar riffs and insistent drums unlike any cover the duo had heard before. It was intoxicating, bewitching even. And then the singer moved. 

He twisted and writhed, as if pulled by invisible strings. His body arched and contorted with the melody in a way that went beyond physical skill or enthusiastic stage antics. It was like his every bone was liquid under his skin, each undulation and snap perfectly synchronized with the music, each contortion expressing the pure, raw emotion of the song.

His eyes were something else entirely. They were filled with his soul's vividness, his pupils expanded to an uncharacteristic size. An otherwise bright blue was flecked with an unnatural gold. His gaze shot through the crowd like a bolt of lightning, drawn to every stare, every face, leaving them in a dizzy trance.

Jake swallowed hard. "I see it." He admitted. Jeremy flashed a triumphal smirk as Jake continued, "It's like his body is just... not his own when the music starts. It's actually quite fascinating."

Jeremy nodded. "It's incredible. Like... primeval or something. He's not playing for us, he's kind of just... with the music."

The crowd seemed to share their sentiment. The room was enthralled, drawn into the spectacle before them. The singer's voice was like a magnet, his stage performance a spectacle, and everyone was trapped deep within the magnetic field.

As the night continued, Jake and Jeremy forgot that they were there to see a live band. Instead, they found themselves watching a spectacle that was part opera, part ballet, and part ritual. They were witnessing something that was more than just music. It was an energy, a performative possession, the transmutation of a man into something beyond humanity through the medium of song. The singer served as a conduit, a kind of musical shaman guiding the audience into a shared experience of something inexplicably otherworldly.

When the show finally ended, Jake and Jeremy walked out into the cool night air, the singer's final howl still reverberating in their hearts and bones. 

"And?" Jeremy asked. 

Jake shrugged and replied, "Possessed or not, that was the best damn show I've seen in a long time." They both laughed a little, the surreal magic of the gig hanging in the air between them, their senses tingling as if they'd just woken from an incredibly vivid dream. Their night had been anything but ordinary.

Adams, had a monocle and a stuffy British accent. It was just one of those silly things we teased her about, in between algebraic fractions and linear equations. Every now and then, when the pressure of a lesson would lessen, someone would weakly attempt the British accent and we'd all crack up like it was the funniest thing ever. It was our way of coping with the fact that we couldn't comprehend half of what she taught. 

Mrs. Adams, being the good sport that she was, would humor us by putting on the thickest British accent she could muster and dramatically demanding that we 'get on with it'. The sound of her feigned accent combined with the thought of her sporting a monocle was enough to send us into fits of giggles - until she wiped the smile off our faces with an unexpected pop quiz.

Despite our silliness and the frequent laughter, she never stopped teaching or asked us to grow up. She made us learn, even when we thought we were unteachable. She persistently powered through, even when our teenage mockery threatened to veer or distract her. Sometimes, her cool professionalism in those moments irritated us - it was like her resolve was a wall we couldn't breach.

Many years later, at our 20-year high school reunion, we found out that Mrs. Adams had been battling cancer all those years she taught us. She was ill, in pain, and heavily medicated but she continued teaching, continuing challenging us.

Suddenly, the laughter didn't feel so light-hearted anymore. Our ignorant jests and immature humor seemed so insignificant, cheap even. I wish we had known then, so we could have thanked her. Against all odds, despite her poor health and our offensive humor, Mrs. Adams was always there, teaching us the very essence of determination and resilience amongst quadratic equations and theorems.

From beyond the grave, Mrs. Adams had taught us the most important lesson of all – life's harshest equations aren't solved in the comfort of a well-lit classroom; they're solved in the trenches of adversity, with the unrelenting will to keep moving forward. 

Ironically, her teachings made more sense now than they ever did in the classroom. Mrs. Adams, with her fictitious monocle and feigned British accent, had been our greatest teacher. Not just in mathematics but in life.

"Certainly," the speaker said, adjusting their glasses as they flipped open a worn, old notebook. "So, as I was saying, despite his occasional lack of clarity, he had an odd sort of cleverness about him. It didn't show itself often or loudly, but in the quiet moments, the humdrum, everyday routines, you could catch glimpses of it."

They took a sip of their drink before continuing, their eyes lost in the past.

"He was never good with the big picture or complex equations," the speaker admitted, a nostalgic grin tugging at the corners of their mouth. "But he had an uncanny knack for understanding people. Seeing right through their pretences, their facades, and getting straight to the heart of who they really were. It was as if he couldn't understand anything else, but he could read people like open books."

The room fell silent for a moment, absorbing the speaker's words. Then someone stirred, broke the silence. "And? What happened to him?" 

The speaker sighed, leaning back in their chair, their smile turning bittersweet. 

"In a way, his ability to see through people became his downfall. It made him lonely, cynical. He believed that because he could see the worst in people, others could see the same in him. So he isolated himself, chose solitude over company. In the end, his unique gift ended up turning into his own personal hell." 

The room was silent again, filled with immense sadness for the dense but wise man they'd just learned about.

"Poor guy," someone eventually whispered, breaking the silence.

"Yes," the speaker agreed softly. "But I believe he wouldn't have had it any other way. After all, we're all a little damaged in our own ways. His way just happened to be a little more visible than most."

I am lost, or perhaps purposely hiding, in the obscure crevices of existence. I don't know if this note will find its way into the right hands. Maybe it will, or maybe it will drift forever in the purgatory of forgotten words. Regardless, I've written it, this scream silenced within the simulating calm of black ink and white paper. I've summoned the courage to strip my soul naked and bare before unsympathetic eyes. Perhaps the very act of writing this is a testament to some small ember of hope still stubbornly glowing within me, a proof that my soul is still alive beneath the despair that has so thoroughly claimed me.

If you find this and you don't know who I am, then please continue. Don't try to understand my suffering, for it is as unique as the intricate patterns of a snowflake. Each one different, delicately complex in its simplicity. Instead, fill your day with the light of your life. Cherish the chances that are still offered to you. Embrace the love that envelopes you. Breathe the sweet air that is denied to me. Enjoy the simple gratification of waking up to sunlight streaming into your eyes each morning. Love and hope and fight with all the vigor of someone who knows their worth.

If you find this and you know me, then please continue. Forgive me for burdening you with my despair. Love your life for both of us. Revel in the joy of existence a little more passionately, laugh a little louder, dream a little farther.

They were trying to concentrate on the blueprints spread out before them, but their mind kept drifting away. The intricate designs of the building they were supposed to be working on were normally enough to captivate Sky, but today was different.

Frustration etched its way onto their face as they ran a hand through their messy brown hair, trying again to focus their attention on the task at hand. Their desk was cluttered, much like their thoughts - pens and pencils scattered haphazardly, papers loosely strewn around, a half-empty cup of coffee balanced precariously on the edge.

The clock on the wall ticked away mercilessly, highlighting the passage of time like a cruel joke. Sky’s gaze shifted towards it frequently, as if hoping to see that more time had passed than actually had. They hadn’t done nearly enough work, and the deadline rapidly approached. 

Suddenly, their phone buzzed, a welcome distraction from the stress of their job. The caller ID showed it was Alex, their partner. Answering it, Sky forced a smile onto their face, “Hey, you’re on speaker, what’s up?”

They heard a sigh from the other end, then Alex's voice sounded in the small room, "Just checking in on you. It sounds like you're working yourself into the ground... again."

Sky looked away from the blueprints, gazing out of the window instead. Their fingers kept tapping on the desk, a rhythm all too familiar in moments of stress. No mention of the call's purpose, just the truth sitting there, waiting for Sky to admit it.

"Yeah," they finally said into the silence, their voice barely a whisper, "I think I am." They stared blankly at the cityscape outside their window, fear about deadlines momentarily replaced with the comfort of Alex's voice. "But I’ll deal with it, won't I?"

And even in the face of mounting pressure and potential failure, that was the only certainty Sky had. They picked up their pen and turned back to the blueprints, determined to face it head-on. Their determination echoed in the consoling silence that their partner left them with, trusting Sky to know their own strength.

In the end, the ticking clock didn't seem to be so mocking anymore. It was just a marker of time. And as the sun began to set, Sky spilled more ink on the plans, with each passing tick of the clock signifying their steady progress.

The simpering snorts and derisive looks from the lumbering hulks in the orc village didn't faze Clugo anymore. His muscular physique from his youth had softened into a rotund belly, but his mind had sharpened like a spearhead. He no longer sought to prove his worth in the hunt or the combat ring, but in the quieter, more contemplative spaces filled with age-worn parchments and dusty scrolls. His throne was his reading chair tucked into a sunny corner of the library, and his kingdom was the knowledge he had amassed over the years. 

The grand library was located in the heart of the village, its existence an anomaly in the otherwise brawny, brutish orc society. It was his haven, his sanctuary. The vast expanse was filled with the aroma of dry parchment and old stories. It was a cacophony of silent voices awaiting to tell their tales, and Clugo was their devoted audience. 

Each day started with Clugo enthusiastically flitting through the labyrinth of bookshelves. He manoeuvred through the library with a dexterity none could attribute to his seemingly clumsy heartiness. His eyes, gleaming like jade, devoured every word, every sentence, imbibing tales of courage, heroics, and loss. The chronicles of his ancestors, the stories of the world beyond his village, secrets of arcane science and magic — they were all pieces of a colossal puzzle that he yearned to complete.

While the other orcs honed their bodies to perfection, marred with scars of prideful battles, Clugo walked a different path. He trained his mind. He brewed ideas, stitched stories, and painted vivid images in his head—all with the magic of his words.

The other villagers didn't understand his soft-spoken passion for history or his enthusiasm for the intricate workings of magic; Clugo never expected them to. In their eyes, he was a small, plump, soft-hearted orc—unfit for battle, unworthy of the hunt, an outsider among his kind. But in his heart, Clugo knew he was a warrior—his battles fought with intellect, his hunts within the recesses of knowledge. 

Despite the shadows of critique shrouding him, he remained unfazed, for Clugo—the small plump orc—was the keeper of the grand library, the narrator of their lineage, the chronicler of their existence. To him, it wasn't about the size of his muscles or the scars on his body; it was the vastness of his mind, the courage in his soul, and the kindness in his heart that defined him. And he was determined to leave his legacy in the heart of their history, embedded in the words and the stories of his grand library.

As soon as I crossed the threshold, the stench of burning incense and old animal hides stung my nostrils, causing me to recoil. The floor was strewn with strange tinctures, purples, greens, and yellows liquids bubbling in odd-shaped glass containers and cauldrons spread over the stone floors.

The room was draped with a thick, buzzing silence that seemed unnatural. Illustrations of magical glyphs and celestial constellations adorned the walls, and stacks of weather-beaten books, all brimming with potent spells and arcane knowledge unknown to mankind, were haphazardly thrown around.

In the middle of the room rested a heavy wooden table, its surface scrubbed raw from countless spells gone wrong. Mismatched vials, rusty iron tools, old quills, and crumbled scrolls spoke of a recent ritual; the implications of which I shuddered to comprehend.

Cautiously, I ascended the winding staircase that spiraled up towards the tower's peak. The distinct hum of magical energy grew stronger as I climbed higher. Strange shapes moved in my peripheral vision, ghosts of spells long past, that reacted to my presence with ethereal whispers that swirled around the chilly air.

Arriving at the topmost room, I found a sight that would chill the bones of the most hardy adventurers. A whimsically chaotic workspace, if you could call it that, filled with objects of unknown, potentially dangerous purpose. A massive grimoire, leather binding worn and aged, lay open under the quicksilver glow of an ethereal light. Suddenly, a warped laughter echoed from below, reverberating off the close stone walls. Startled, I quickly retreated into the shadows. This was surely the notorious hedge wizard, master of eldritch arts, returning from his errands. Now, hiding in the shadows, I observed and documented, ready to spread the knowledge of the horrors I had seen for those brave or foolish enough to venture close to this forbidden tower.

I am intrigued by your comment about a 'sleepy conscience.' It reminds me of the idea that some people are not fully aware, or awake, to their ethical responsibilities and actions. This could be due to a variety of reasons, including lack of self-reflection, avoidance of guilt or shame, or simply a lack of moral development.

A person with a 'sleepy conscience' might easily turn a blind eye to their misdeeds or fail to recognize the harm they've caused to others. In extreme cases, they might deny their wrongdoing altogether, which is a defense mechanism often used by individuals who can't deal with the cognitive dissonance between their self-perception and their actual behavior.

I believe that awakening a 'sleepy conscience' often involves efforts to enhance empathy, self-awareness, and moral reasoning. Therapy or mentoring can play a significant role in this, as it allows individuals to confront their actions and understand their impacts on others.

One common way to activate the conscience is through perspective-taking activities that build empathy, like reading narratives that provide insights into other people's experiences and feelings. Another method is through cultivating self-awareness by encouraging self-reflection on personal values and beliefs.

Moral reasoning, the cognitive process of deciding what is right and wrong, can also be developed with practices like ethical dilemmas discussions, which force individuals to consider different perspectives and potential consequences of their actions.

In conclusion, while a 'sleepy conscience' might initially seem like a hindrance, it can serve as an opportunity for growth if recognized and dealt with properly. It may not be an easy process, but awakening the conscience can lead to profound personal transformation and enriched relationships with others.

The sound of gushing water eventually stopped, plunging us into an eerie silence. We then started working on cleaning up the mess. Armed with every towel and mop we could find, we launched a counterattack against the flooding water.

In the face of inconvenience, we had learned to stick together, just two against the world and now against a mass of murky soapy water. And despite the tiredness setting in, we still managed to share a laugh or two about the absurdity of the situation. After all, memories – both good and bad – have a funny way of bringing people closer. And that night certainly went down as one of our most unforgettable ones. Despite the fatigue and the ruined game night, we knew it was a story we would be telling years down the line. 

Indeed, that was an evening we'd remember every time we passed a Laundromat.

I had always felt... different, as if I was abruptly disconnected from the symphony of life that played in vibrant harmony around me. It was a sensation hard to articulate, like silently watching an opera in a language unknown; intrigued, yet distanced by its cryptic melody. 

I was born in a typical household - a father who loved baseball, a mother who breathed poetry and a younger brother who, I swear, was conceived to be my personal nemesis - a white picket fence American family. Yet, within this precious frame of ordinary life, I was the offbeat echo.

I was the child who preferred the solace of faded paperbacks to the boisterous huddles of neighborhood kids, the teenager who found the company of stars more meaningful than school dances, and now, an adult who felt more at ease amidst arcane artifacts and ancient dust in history museums than the bustling, unforgiving corporate world.

My parents were understanding, their love was undeterred by their gradually blooming comprehension of my offbeat nature. But as supportive as they were, I often wondered if they ever awake in the immense midnight silence, questioning their gene pool's creation of such an unconventional anomaly.

Childhood friends, their young minds unable to grasp my introverted passion, soon fell away like autumn leaves. I was not lonely though, for I had rivers of ink that could compose sonnets and literary worlds that offered countless adventures. I was not lonely, yet sometimes, I yearned for a human presence who could voluntarily, without obligation, comprehend my enigmatic existence.

It was not that my ideas were radical, or my vision, revolutionary. It was not that I was draped in an aura of exceptional genius. I was just... different. Different in the way I perceived my surroundings, different in the way I responded, different in the way I existed.

I figured it was a result of some cosmic hiccup - a minor glitch in the assembly line of human production. A quirk that made me simultaneously grateful and aggrieved. Nevertheless, it had one irrefutable virtue - it was mine. My own weird, complex, baffling identity.

Above all, I realized that it is our peculiar idiosyncrasies that shape our journeys, fashioning them into an intricate ballet of treasured moments. And so, I embraced my eccentricity, no longer viewing it as an aberration, but as a testament of my unique impression on this vast canvas of life.

I had always felt different. But now, I understood that it wasn't a curse, but a gift permitting me to journey on an unbeaten path. Different indeed, but never alone, for in the depths of my heart, the universe composed a symphony that only I could understand. And, perhaps, that was my purpose, my contribution to the grand opera of life.

"When we step onto that red, alien soil, we'll be pioneers. A new breed of explorers marking the dawn of interplanetary civilization," they said.

The promise of new discoveries, untouched landscapes, the thrill of advancing science, technology, and potentially even society was exhilarating. It was this very speech from the mission director that motivated some of the brightest minds around the globe to register for the Mars colonization program.

The training was grueling, the preparation was exhaustive. Some of us, admittedly, were even considering pulling out. But we held on; for science, for discovery, for the slight chance of experiencing a life that millions, or possibly billions, could only dream of.

The day finally came when we blasted into orbit, leaving Earth and all its splendors behind. The journey was filled with isolation, bouts of homesickness, and occasional panic at the sheer distance we were covering from our home planet.

When we finally arrived, we found Mars to be, quite starkly, the epitome of wilderness. The deep, dusty red landscape stretched for miles, mountains formed clusters in parts, valleys sunk deep, while sandstorms occasionally whipped up madness. The dunes were shifting, changing patterns like glittering russet sequins under the ceaseless scrutiny of Phobos and Deimos, the two Martian moons.

"Mars will be great," they promised. We found out quickly that 'great' had many versions. It was great, indeed, but in an alien, menacing, and unpredictable kind of way.

We learned to adapt. We constructed habitats, grew our own food, and dug deep into the ground for water. Within our pressurized modules, life seemed almost normal—a bit of the Earth ingrained on an alien planet. We wore the planetary suits, ventured out into the harsh Martian environment and absorbed every detail.

Mars was never like Earth, nor could it ever be. The red planet did not welcome us with open arms, rather it tested our resilience, innovation, and sanity.

"Mars will be great"... Those words echoed, a taunting reminder of the romanticized dream we once had. It was great but in a totally different aspect - it was raw, it was cruel and it was merciless. It tested us to our limits, pushed our boundaries, and presented us with challenges we never thought we could overcome.

Yet in the light of the sunsets, a blue hue unlike any seen on Earth, we found a strange comfort. In the silence that wrapped around us during the Martian nights, we discovered our own strength. We found beauty in adversity, courage in desolation, and purpose in survival.

"Mars is great," we would say now. Because Mars is not just a planet, but a testament to our spirit, adaptability, and the indomitable human will to go beyond and conquer the unknown.

"Mars is great," indeed.

Adrift in a sea of hopelessness, he moved aimlessly through the city, feeling perpetually like an outsider looking in. Without a job, family or prospects, he struggled to conceive a purpose for each new day. Hunger ate at his belly and pale fear nibbled at the edges of his sanity.

Once, he had a job. He remembered the surge of satisfaction he felt, the first time he held his paycheck. The pride he felt, handling the hard-earned money, taking care of his family. But then, everything spiraled out of control. The company downsized, and he was on the streets, a stark reality he hadn’t seen coming.

Without a job, month after month, his savings dwindled to nothing. The confident, cheerful man he used to be was now just a hollow shell of his former self. The laughter and joy he shared with his family seemed like a distant echo. His wife left him, taking their two children, unable to bear their rapidly declining living condition.

They were his everything, his motivation to work hard, to strive and never give up. Now, they were gone. It felt like his heart was ripped off his chest. It was almost unbearable to have his children, his life, ripped away like that. Despair settled in like a thick, crushing fog.

The memories of his past life felt like shards of glass, pieced together to form a picture of utter agony and desolation. Was there a way out? He had no comfort from family, no help tinged with the warmth of familiarity. He was now a man without roots, unanchored and lost in the rough sea of life.

The city was no longer a welcoming haven; it was a colossal monolith of relentless indifference. Every face seemed indifferent, exacerbating the cold void in his heart.

Despite all the despair, he had two choices— either succumb to the crushing pressure or battle the storm. He chose to fight; resigned to his fate, he did not intend to go down without a fight. He would do everything in his power to claw his way back into the world that had cruelly discarded him.

With this newfound resolve, he started looking for jobs, every rejection a leaden weight, but he soldiered on. He kept reminding himself - If fate had turned against him, he would fight back.

At night, under the dimly lit stars, he dreamt of his children. In the morning, he woke up with an iron determination to do better, whatever it took. He was not looking for mercy nor sympathy; bare perseverance and obstinate determination would pull him out of this pit, he believed. 

No job. No family. No prospects. Yet, despite his desolation, he would survive, he would thrive, because he had something to hold on, hope. Hope was a spark in the depths of his despair, a spark that refused to die. It nourished his spirit, promising a future better than his harsh present. 

And it was this steadfast belief in a better future that kept him going, day after desperate day... A man without a job, a family, or prospects. But, never without hope.

Despite their incredible strength and the fearsome myths surrounding them, gorillas are often misunderstood and misrepresented. They are intelligent creatures and are naturally inclined towards peaceful behaviors. Their strength is primarily used in their natural habitat, the vast areas of tropical forests in Africa, to defend themselves from threats or intruders and to search for food, not to engage in aggressive acts against humans.

Known to be the largest of the great apes, gorillas are powerful and robust, with bodies designed to easily navigate their forest homes. Their arms are longer than their legs, and they exhibit tremendous dexterity with their hands and fingers, much like humans. Males, in particular, have broader chests and shoulders, with a characteristic silver-grey section of fur on their lower backs earning them the term "silverbacks." This strength, however, is not what defines them.

Gorillas are intelligent, emotional, and social beings who live in close-knit family groups led by a dominant male. They express a wide range of emotions and can show empathy, grief, compassion, and even laughter. They communicate through a variety of complex vocalizations, gestures, and facial expressions, highlighting their remarkable cognitive abilities.

Despite being herbivores, gorillas are not to be taken lightly. They possess the physical ability to do great harm if they feel threatened or if their family group is put in danger. However, unprovoked attacks are highly unlikely. In fact, gorillas often display 'mock' displays of aggression, like chest beating and charging, rather than actual violent behavior, as a way to avoid violence.

Their strength goes beyond their physical attributes. They have a poignant resilience, persisting in the face of continuous habitat loss due to illegal logging, mining, and human encroachment. They are a poignant symbol of the beauty and fragility of our world's wildlife, reminding us of both nature's raw power and the need for our compassion and care.

So, while gorillas are indeed mightily impressive beasts, to boil them down to their capacity for danger does them a disservice. Much like humans, they use their strength and intelligence to live, love, protect, and survive in an increasingly threatened world. Their true strength is not just in their muscle - it is in their ability to endure.

The room was clinical, almost blindingly so, and it was devoid of any furniture. As my eyes adjusted, I noticed a subtle but noticeable hum that vibrated through my feet, almost inaudible but undeniable. I looked down, noticing the floor was opaque and glowing faintly beneath me, as if it was made of some divine phosphorus.

A sense of imminent dread gripped me. This wasn't the place I had left, the little cozy nook with the worn-out leather couch and the books that I owned. This was something alien, something I had never witnessed before.

Despite my fear, I forced myself to move forward, my footsteps echoing in the empty room. After a few steps, I came face to face with a mirror mounted on the wall. Reflected in the glass was a face that was both familiar and foreign - my own, but subtly changed. My eyes had an eerie glowing hue to them, and my skin seemed... translucent.

Suddenly, the mirror shifted, melting away to reveal another room on the other side. It was a complete contrast to the room I was in - darkness spread across it, the only light coming from numerous tiny screens floating in mid-air.

Feeling a strange pull, I stepped through the mirror, the glassy surface rippling as I crossed over. The faint hum from before was replaced with a multitude of whispers, emanating from the tiny screens. Each had different images - places I've been, people I've known, moments I'd lived through.

Suddenly it dawned on me. I was inside my own mind. The sterile room was my conscious mind - orderly, structured. The room with the floating screens was my subconscious mind - chaotic, layered.

Fear gave way to fascination as I realized that I was privy to a world unexplored, the world within me. But before I could explore further, the screens began flickering, and the whispers grew louder, merging into a cacophony of sound.

And as I looked on with a newfound understanding, the screens began to show the same image - a locked wooden door. The subconscious, it seemed, was guiding me towards something, something hidden deep within my psyche.

Summoning my courage, I reached out to one of the screens, and just as before - the screen rippled under my touch revealing the door in front of me. A door, to what reality or memory, I had yet to find out.

With a deep breath, I laid my hand on the doorknob, turned, and entered the unknown. There was only one thing certain: I was embarking on a journey inward like none other.

As I stepped further into the room, the somber tones of old wood and dust filled my nostrils. The room was cluttered with dusty books and papers strewn about the place in reckless abandon. Strange contraptions of metal and glass, twining together in a chaotic confusion of shapes and sizes, filled up most of the space. 

"George?" I tried once more, a whisper among the silent stillness. Only the echo of my own voice answered back. Anxiety knotted my stomach as I tread deeper into his sanctum of scientific experiments.

I turned my attention to a desk at the far end of the room. On it lay a smudge of ink, a paper weighted with a half-empty glass of whiskey and a pen fallen clumsily upon the thick pile of notes. I moved towards it, walking carefully between the maze of contraptions, my heartbeat pounding in my ears.

As I reached the desk, my eyes skimmed across the paper. Diagrams and notes were scribbled across it hurriedly, betraying George's normally meticulous handwriting. Something caught the corner of my eye, a note stuffed under the main pile”

'...In case of my abrupt absence, go to the safe behind the largest portrait...' The note said. A cold chill ran down my spine. I quickly turned around, scanning the room for the aforementioned portrait. A large, ornate frame hung lonesomely at one end, depicting a stern-looking man with piercing eyes.

Without wasting a moment, I hastened towards it and moved it aside. Behind the portrait, concealed in the wall, was a small safe. It required a combination. Luckily, George had scribbled it down at the bottom of the note. With trembling fingers, I put in the code and with a soft click, the safe door opened. 

Inside, there was another note and a peculiar device I didn’t recognize. I clutched the note and unfolded it, a sense of foreboding hanging heavily in the air.

'Do not forget, our survival depends on this…'

Suddenly, the room felt colder. I looked at the small object inside the safe with a newfound sense of urgency and fear. It seemed my search for George was just the beginning.

"Explain," God said, His voice resonating throughout the divine space, the gentleness in His tone not hiding the immense power behind it. His demanding eyes were fixed on Michael with a stern, yet reassuring look. 

"Firstly," Michael cleared his throat, preparing to delve into the current state of affairs, "our emissary angels on Earth report an increasing sense of uncertainty among humans. They pray more fervently, their faith seems to waver between abject fear and hopeful resilience."

"Isn't that the nature of mankind, Michael?" God interjected, His eyes shimmering with profound understanding. "They crumble, they pray, their faith is tested and then it grows stronger. Isn't that how they've always evolved?"

Michael nodded, "Indeed, but we are registering a higher frequency of negative emotions. Doubt, fear, anger. And the balance of the spiritual energies is not at its usual equilibrium which gives rise to the concern."

God took in the information, His ever-calm spectral face revealing no worries, just fostering contemplation. "And the physical realm?" He asked.

"Yes," Michael moved on, "several areas on Earth are being subjected to environmental shifts. Natural disasters, according to human understanding, are currently on the rise. Also, a more threatening issue at hand is their misuse of resources, accelerating the climate changes."

As Michael relayed the ongoing happenings on Earth, God’s eyes seemed to darken, giving away His concern. He sat back in His heavenly throne, His thoughts drenched with the welfare of His creation.

“These are challenging times for my children. The trials they are to face will test their faith, their humanity," God muttered more to Himself than to Michael.

"Yes," Michael agreed, closing the portfolio solemnly. "We will continue to guide them, in hope they find the strength to make better choices."

Heaven stood silent then, the celestial entities acknowledging the severity of the situation while God contemplated His next move.

Dr. Anika Carter had been an eye surgeon for nearly a decade, and yet no patient’s case had ever piqued her interest as Emily Harris. Emily was a congenitally blind woman engaged to a man she had never seen. Her fiancé, Tom, had spent years saving up for an operation that could potentially restore Emily's sight. He was hopeful that the world through Emily's new eyes would include him.

As Dr. Carter walked down the sterile hallways, she replayed the conversation with Emily during their preliminary consultation. The young woman had spoken with a gentle voice, full of nervous anticipation yet calm acceptance. When asked what her biggest fear was, Emily candidly replied, “That I won't be able to recognize Tom.” This hadn't just moved Dr. Carter; it had inspired her.

She pushed open the door to the pre-op room, her shoes clicking against the tiled floor, her heartbeat echoing with excitement and, yes, a hint of apprehension. She closed her eyes, steadied her breath, and fixed her focus on the task. She’d been part of medical miracles before, but never one as personal as this.

Her calming confidence offered stark contrast to Emily’s anxious vulnerability, designed to put her patient at ease. But there, lying on the hospital bed bathed in fluorescent lighting, Emily’s face expressed not fear but quiet courage. The faith in her future, in the promise of seeing her world, her life ahead was clearly reflected in the serenity on her face. 

“Are you ready, Emily?” Dr. Carter asked, coating her professional demeanor with genuine warmth. Emily simply nodded, the corners of her lips curving into a brave smile.

As Dr. Carter positioned her surgical tools, her mind focused on the precision each movement required. Her objective: to restore a woman's vision, to unveil the unseen, to enrich a life, to allow love to flourish visually. 

Hours passed, filled with diligent, exacting work guided by technology and expertise. Dr. Carter remained steady, thorough, and undeterred. Her hands moved like a symphony, each action calculated and precise. As she concluded the operation, she felt a surge of optimism and triumph. Now, all that remained was to wait for Emily’s post-op recovery.

Days later, when Emily opened her eyes and recognized Tom’s face from his soft voice, Dr. Carter witnessed first-hand the miracle she had envisioned. The indescribable joy radiating from Emily as she admired Tom's face for the first time was an affirmation for all the years Dr. Carter had devoted to her profession. Indeed, it was moments like these that made all the sacrifices of a surgeon’s life worthwhile.

Helping Emily see was not merely another successful surgery for Dr. Carter. It was a reminder that the blend of science and human spirit could indeed create beautiful miracles. A previously unseen world opened up for Emily, and in the process, new perspectives opened for Dr. Carter too, ones she’d carry forever in her own vision of life and career.

It was 12:56 AM and evacuation horns started blaring, filling the dead of night with chilling cacophony. The ambient red light spat out by the emergency evacuation signs colored the streets blood-red, hinting at the disaster that was yet unfurling.

I leapt from my bed, tripping over the scattered leftovers from the previous day - student textbooks, a half-eaten piece of toast, some crumpled paper balls. Fortunately, I managed to catch myself before I fully elicited the wrath of the wooden floorboards. The howl of the alarm hadn't ceased its horrific harmony, persisting in inducing a sense of irrevocable dread.

Pulling myself together, I snatched some essentials. I ended up with a flashlight, an extra set of clothes, my wallet, and my late father’s pocket knife. It seemed wise to stuff everything into a rucksack and take it with me. The weight felt oddly reassuring in the uncertainty of the moment, perhaps a false sense of control while the world cascaded into chaos.

Out on the streets, people streamed by in panicked droves, each face reflecting its own snapshot of terror and confusion. The once-sleepy town echoed with the evacuation horns and screams of the displaced townsfolk, a terrifying cacophony that only amplified the unease in my gut.

The episodic, horrified shouts, pleaded questions to the divine, barking orders given out by the authorities, all merged into a nightmarish symphony — a dire requiem for the peaceful life we had known all along. 

Too many questions boldly shot through my mind with an alarming alacrity, yet I didn't have the time to answer any. What had triggered the evacuation? Was it a natural disaster? Or a man-made catastrophe? Neither the sleepy town nor its quaint folks, including myself, were prepared for anything of this magnitude.

Racing down the streets, red light-tears running down the sides of the buildings, clutching my rucksack to my chest like a shield against the unfolding chaos, I realized that life wouldn't be the same again. The screeching horns served as a wake-up call not only from late-night sleep but also from the blissful ignorance we'd been dwelling in.

It was indeed 12:56 AM when my quiet existence was replaced by panic-filled restlessness. I barely acknowledged the passage of time, for in the face of certain peril, time tends to lose its relevance. All I had was the will to survive, the determination to escape the clutches of a disaster whose face remained hidden in the crimson chaos of evacuation.

That night, at precisely 12:56 AM, everything changed.

Your parents may have noticed the persistent ringing or buzzing noise in your ears and diagnosed it as tinnitus. This is a common condition, especially as one grows older. It can be caused by various factors like exposure to loud noise, aging, ear injury or a circulatory system disorder.

Often tinnitus isn't a sign of something serious but it can be very irritating or even debilitating for some people. Unfortunately, there's no cure for tinnitus, but there are treatments that can help reduce the impact of the noise on your life. 

Lifestyle changes like avoiding loud noises, limiting caffeine and alcohol, stopping smoking, managing stress, and regular exercise can all help. If these don't help, then it's best to consult a doctor who can recommend treatments like hearing aids, sound therapy, or behavioral therapy.

It's important though to keep in mind that everyone's experience with tinnitus is different, so what works for one person might not work for another. It can take time to find the best treatment, but many people can find relief.

Doubts and questions swirled around like a mini hurricane in my head. Should it be a profound question about the meaning of life or a silly question like what would happen if pigs could fly? I decided to break down my dilemma into categories: personal, world-altering and absurd questions. 

Personal questions were deeply related to me, like what my life would look like if I had pursued music, or if I had married my high-school sweetheart. These seemed selfish; after all, the "What-If?" machine could answer questions that might have severe implications on knowledge and history. 

World-altering questions were another realm altogether. What if Hitler won the war? What if the technological revolution never happened? These questions were alluring, but they bore a heavy responsibility. The answers could be utterly disturbing and change how we perceived history. 

The absurd questions were meant purely for the pleasure of curiosity – what if humans had tails or what if dinosaurs still roamed the Earth. They were certainly fun to think about, but they didn’t seem worth wasting my one chance, my one question.

However, there was a fourth category. A category which seemed to overlap across the other three. A category that contained questions that were a bit personal, could be world-altering, and were the perfect blend of absurdly refreshing. 

After continued contemplation, I concluded my question would fall under this category. The machine hummed gently as I cleared my throat. My heart pounded wildly at the anticipation, the endless possibilities of the machine's answer. 

Steeling myself, I took a deep breath, then asked, "What if everyone in the world could read everyone else's mind?" The machine whirred in response, lights flickering as it processed the information. Little did I know, the answer to this simple question would change everything.

The voices were his reality, much like the shadows were the only reality known to the inhabitants of the cave in Plato’s Allegory. For him, the voices were his only source of knowledge, his only touch of reality. Others may see it as an illness, an affliction, a tragedy, but for him, it was the only world he had ever known. 

Just like the cave dwellers, he didn’t have real physical objects around him. He was trapped in his mind, chained up by the voices that controlled him. His reality was constructed by these voices, by their whispers and screams, their chatting and pleading, their condemnation and approval. Every perception, every experience was mediated through them. 

Occasionally, when the voices were kind, when they lifted him up rather than pulled him down, he would ponder the existence of a greater reality - a world beyond the voices, beyond the constraints of his mind. But these thoughts brought more terror than relief. The concept of a world outside his mind was unbearable. It was an unknown territory, a place of uncertainty and chaos.

For him, the voices were not the darkness of the cave but the fire casting shadows on the wall. Ignorance was not his problem; comfort within his own chains was. He clung to the voices, to the safety and familiarity of his mind.

Every once in a while, a psychiatrist would enter his reality, much like the philosopher who ventured outside Plato’s cave. They would try to lead him out of his inner world, to release him from his self-built prison. He would resist, fearing the blindness that might come from the bright and chaotic reality of the world outside his mind.

These voices, although troublesome and disruptive, were his only company, his only companions in the isolation of his existence. Their constant presence reminded him that he was alive, that he existed.

In essence, he was not living in a cave, but a fortress of his own creation, built from the voices inside his head. Like Plato's cave dwellers, he, too, was a prisoner to his restricted worldview. But unlike them, he held the key to his own chains. The challenge then, was not escaping his reality, but accepting the existence of another. Once he embraced the existence of a world beyond the voices, he could move towards understanding and additional clarity. And just like the philosopher in Plato's allegory, he could then freely explore the world around him, without fear or trepidation.

Inside the conference room, the atmosphere was tense. These were not your typical delegates in crisp suits and polished shoes. Instead, they were dragon folk - beings who could transform between human and dragon forms at will. The conference table was a gigantic slab of charred obsidian, glimmering ominously under the warm, flickering glow of torches along the walls. Huge banners and tapestries, engraved with ancient sigils representing different clans, hung proudly in the grand hall.

At the head of the table sat Drakon, the oldest and wisest amongst them. With scales shimmering like opals under the torchlight and eyes that held a millennium's worth of wisdom, he watched over the proceedings with a judicious gaze. His human form was an elderly man, graceful yet sturdy, with a sharp mind that belied his advancing age. 

Seated around the table were the representatives of the major dragon clans. Each bore the distinctive characteristics of their lineage, from the frost-blue scales of the Iceflight clan to the raging red eyes of the Flameborn ones. Their human forms were just as diverse, from burly warriors to sleek strategists, radiating an elemental power that kept even the rowdiest of them in check.

Taara of the Skyweavers clan was the first to break the silence. Small as she was fierce, her sapphire eyes blazed as she addressed the room. "Our territories are being encroached upon, our hatchlings threatened. We can't remain idle in the face of such provocations!"

"I concur," growled Grane, a representative from the Stonehide clan, his voice as grating as gravel tumbling down a mountainside. "Enough is enough; we need to retaliate."

"Retaliation will only lead to more conflict!" countered Ignis of the Flameborn clan, a fiery spark in his crimson eyes. "We need a peaceful resolution."

Voices started rising; scoffs and mutterings filled the air, fueling the already claustrophobic tension in the room. But then Drakon rose, his presence demanding silence. Looking around, he saw the representatives quiet down, the fiery glares subduing under his gaze. "We hold this conference to chart a path of unity and wisdom, not division and discord."

With that, he signaled the meeting to continue, with suggestions and strategies discussed in a more civil and respectful manner. Peaceful or otherwise, the dragonfolk had a common goal: to protect their kind and ensure their continued existence. And that will was unshakeable, burning brighter than any dragon flame.

Absolutely! Where we left off, we were talking about personal development and the importance of setting realistic goals.

Setting realistic goals begins with making sure they're specific. For better visualization of your objective, using parameters like numbers, percentages, or other detailed descriptions to make your goal as specific as possible is beneficial. For example, instead of the vague goal of "losing weight," a more specific goal might be "lose five pounds in six weeks."

It's also crucial to divide your larger goal into smaller, more manageable objective steps. Breaking down your goals can make them less daunting and more achievable. For example, if you aim to write a full-length novel, you can break that down into smaller goals such as writing a certain number of words each day.

Setting a timeline for each goal is also important. This helps keep you motivated and ensures you stay on track.

Remember, personal development is a journey that does not happen overnight. It takes patience, dedication and hard work. But with realistic goals and proper planning, you can reach your aims.

I made my way across the dimly lit room to the bar. The light from the city seeped in through the blinds, casting long shafts of dim glow that danced on the polished wooden floor, lending an ambient, tranquil and slightly melancholic atmosphere to the space.

I uncorked a bottle of scotch and poured myself a drink, feeling the gear shift in the tension that was until then knitted into the crevices of my furrowed brows. As I placed the bottle back on the shelf, the act told the tale of a ritual that certainly wasn't unfamiliar to me. I lifted the glass in a silent toast to the emptiness that yelped from within the four walls and took a sip, the liquid burning its way down my throat, like a live fire on its path of destruction. 

I trudged towards the window, my weary reflection staring back at me in the glass, overlaid by the sparkling city lights a fair distance away. The sight always reminded me of promises and dreams, both kept and broken. I sipped my drink and grinned, a bitter curve that barely reached my eyes. Just a man and his thoughts, locked in a silent tango, that only the city bore witness to.

My reverie was broken by the buzzing sound of my smartphone. I walked back to the lounge, frowned at the name blinking on the screen, and picked up. The voice on the other end echoed the monotonous hum of work, disrupting the pseudo-serenity of my evening. 

With a long sigh and reluctance stitched into my every movement, I put the half-empty glass down, straightened my back, and began discussing the latest project, every thread of tranquility slowly but surely, transitioning back into the relentless grind of life. Before you heap the usual sympathies upon my soul, let me tell you: this is not a letter of anguish and sorrow. Instead, it is one of hope and promise for the future.

For it is often in death that life truly takes on a beautiful significance. In its finality, it brings an appreciation for the fleeting, fragile moments we've spent on this earth, and a realization of just how precious each one was. It is my hope that you will seize them and live them fully.

At this point, you may wonder why I have chosen to write you this letter. You, my friend, who has been with me through life's paths less traveled, who has seen me in the depths of despair and the heights of joy. I entrust you with this letter because I know you have the heart and the courage to see it realized.

In life, there were certain things that I could not complete, promises left unfulfilled. It is to these promises I now turn. I ask of you a task that I know to be the greatest of burdens.

Firstly, please let my family know of my passing. Lend them your sympathy but remind them that my spirit is with them in every gust of wind that sings in the trees, in every wave that mingles with the shore, in every sunrise and sunset.

I would also ask you to visit my old house. It is a place that holds many dear memories and hollow spaces that echo my laughter. In the attic, you will find a small wooden chest; in this chest are letters I have written for each person who has touched my life. Please ensure that they are delivered appropriately.

In these poems and ramblings, they will find a piece of my spirit and hopefully, a sense of peace. It is these small tokens of love and life that light the days ahead with the warmth of what has been.

It is also my wish that my possessions be sold and all proceeds be donated to the small school on 6th avenue, the one with the red bricked wall, to fund scholarships for underprivileged students. An education can be the most potent weapon and the most beautiful gift.

Finally, the rose in my garden, the one we planted together, please tend to it. Let it bloom, let its fragrance remind the world of a life lived and a friend remembered.

Beyond these requests, I ask you only this. Live! Live your life the way it is meant to be. Chase your dreams with a relentless spirit, gather a thousand beautiful moments and never stop seeking love and peace. Be the best of who you can be, not for anyone else, but for yourself.

My friend, through this letter, I may have died, but I am not gone. Instead, I am dispersed into a thousand particles, scattered by the wind, embedded in the soil, flowing in the river, and twinkling in the stars.

And remember, my dear friend, our lives are not merely flesh and bones, they are a journey, the memories we create, and the love that we leave behind.

Forever with you in spirit,

As I fall onto the cold, ceramic bathroom tiles, my world fades into darkness. A blank abyss, void of sound or sight, swallows me whole. I try to break free, trying to swim towards something solid, something real. But there’s nothing. Just an all-encompassing black void.

Following what feels like an eternity, suddenly, an imaginary sound strikes my eardrums. Faintly at first, it gradually intoxicates my existence. A rhythmic pulsating sound fills the space around me—the echo of my wavering heart beat. It’s the sound of life. My life.

Slowly, my senses awaken, starting from the tips of my fingers. My skin tingled as it touched the cold, hard floor. The faint scent of antiseptic wafts into my consciousness, followed by the taste of stale air on my tongue and the metallic bitterness of blood. The distant murmurers gradually break through the fog, becoming clearer. I realize I’m in hospitals – that’s why the antiseptic smell, and hard floor.

With a surge of power, I attempt to open my eyes, a feat that feels as laborious as lifting a boulder. A painfully bright light blares into my vision, making me squint. The glare slowly turns into diffused shapes, the outlines of people moving about, monitors displaying vital signs, and stark white walls.

I'm in a hospital bed. I'm alive. 

A face comes into focus, a face filled with worry and relief. A sigh escapes my lips and I try to speak, but my cracked lips and parched throat only produce a hoarse whisper. The face leaves my view, replaced by the cold sterility of hospital ceilings. I can hear the rustling of doctors and the murmur of conversations. The world is still a blur but it's real, pulling me deeper into consciousness.

Gradually, memories start to return, in chaotic shards. The morning coffee, the sudden dizziness, the fall, and then the world fading away into emptiness. Anxiety fills me, followed by the firm resolve to fight, to persist, to wake up fully and embrace life again. Yes, I am weak, I am terrified, but I am also alive – and by itself, that is a miracle I am determined to celebrate.

Our race, an unfortunate species known as the Gartopians, was the only one that didn't instinctively understand the concept of common sense.

From the beginning, we were a flawed design. Our creators, the celestial beings known as the Qwyverns, were brilliant in all aspects of existence except one – common sense. They tragically passed on this flaw to us, their most ambitious creation. We, their handmade progeny, evolved to become the most technologically advanced civilization in the galaxy minus an essential survival instinct that every other race was blessed with.

They entrusted us with grand knowledge, unimaginable power, and the ability to traverse the universe, but we lacked the basic understanding of right from wrong, good from bad, the consequence before action - the essence of common sense. And it was this lack that would lead to our downfall.

Our tech developed faster than our society, our wisdom dwarfed by our intelligence. We built ships that could sail through the cosmos, weapons that could obliterate stars, but we lacked the insight to wield them responsibly.

Our lack of common sense often led to reckless ventures, putting our entire civilization in peril. It was common to conduct scientific experiments with an entire city's population unknowingly being the test subjects. The concept of risk assessment, of predicting future outcomes and consequences, simply did not exist among us.

It was no surprise when we ignited civil wars, ignorantly turning our advanced weapons on our own people because we could not foresee the outcomes. Entire cities were wiped out, countless lives were lost, yet we continued on, blind to the destructive path we were forging.

In our fleeting moments of clarity, we sought help from other races. The Yithians, known for their prudence and wisdom, the Fydorians who had harnessed the powers of quantum physics, even the lowly Barath, who were still struggling with basic arithmetic, had something we didn't - the instinctive knowledge of cause and effect.

We tried to learn, to adapt and mimic their simple wisdom, but it was against our nature. Our actions perplexed the other races who gave up on us, seeing us as lost cause. As we were abandoned to our own devices, the despised reality dawned upon us: we were the defective product of the Qwyverns’ creation.

Today, we stand on the precipice of extinction, our once vibrant civilization reduced to ashes, not by a cosmic calamity or ruthless enemies, but by our own hands. As we gaze into the abyss, we realize the bitter truth: the lack of common sense is not just an oversight, but a fatal flaw; a flaw from which we might never recover.

For a moment, I struggled to recall where I was. The last thing I remembered was the overwhelming feeling of exhaustion that swallowed me in the middle of work last night. 

The surroundings weren't familiar. The room was immaculate with bright white walls; a stark contrast to the royal blue curtains that framed the large panoramic window. A dismal white hospital bed lay crumpled, hinting at an unseen struggle.

I attempted to sit up but a sharp pain pierced through my head causing me to wince. I gingerly touched my forehead, feeling a bandage wrapped tightly around it. Reality began to sink in but still, I was clueless about the reasons for my newfound circumstances.

The door to the room creaked open and in walked a nurse, her grey eyes revealing no hint of surprise or concern. In her hand she held a tray with a bowl of what looked like bland hospital food.

"Good morning," she greeted, her voice soft and welcoming, breaking the deafening silence in the room. "How are you feeling?"

I opened my mouth to respond but no sound came out. I cleared my throat and tried again, "Where am I?" It was the first question that could come to my mind.

“You’re in St. Lucia hospital," she informed, placing the tray on the side table. The second question that popped into my head was probably the most obvious one.

"What happened?"

She maintained a professional demeanor as she replied. "You had an accident at work. You struck your head pretty hard and were brought here. You've been asleep for almost a day now."

Suddenly, faint images began to resurface. Late hours, stacks of documents on my desk, a misplaced stapler. I was exhausted and careless, leading to a life-threatening accident, something that seemed so surreal yet terrifyingly possible.

The nurse continued to update me on my condition, but I barely heard anything. All I could think about was how mere exhaustion could lead one to inadvertent disaster.

Days turned into weeks as I recovered, my eyes growing familiar to the daily sight of the two blue curtains and white ceiling. My heart realized the immediacy of rest, the importance of pacing oneself, and the need for a balanced life.

My room, however calming, became a somber reminder of the life left outside the walls of the hospital. The yearning for freedom, the desperation for unwinding, the whimsical urge to appreciate life more vibrantly seeped into my healing soul.

And so, when I finally walked out of the hospital, beneath a sky that had never looked bluer, I knew deep within that my life was ebbing towards a turning point. The experience had etched a stark line in my life - dividing it into 'Before' and 'After'. And as I stared out into the world with renewed vision, I made a promise to myself - never again would I take for granted the beauty and the magnitude of life that lay beyond the blue curtains and the white ceiling.

In the beginning the plan was in full swing, they worked rigorously day in and day out to achieve their common goal. "I'm serious, Matt," I said, staring straight into his horrified blue eyes. "We’re going to run as Independents. We need to stand apart from this corrupt, two-party system."

"But, Sir, the chances of us winning as independents are... is…. it's practically impossible," Matt stuttered, his brain clearly battling between loyalty and sheer disbelief.

"Impossible?" I asked, trying to suppress a smile. "Matt, when we first decided to run, everybody said that we were impossible. An unknown going up against seasoned stalwarts. Yet here we are, merely months away from the election, standing strong and stealing votes from the big-shots. We've always been underdogs, Matt. Our story has always been 'impossible.' If we're going to lose, we should at least lose on our own terms."

I could see his mind turning behind his wide eyes as he processed my words. I reached out, putting a reassuring hand on his shoulder. "Look around you, Matt. The voters aren't happy with either party. They've been lied to, cheated, ignored, used. They deserve someone who is truly fighting for them, not for party supremacy. We can be those people."

"But the logistics, Sir..." he began timidly, clearly still trying to process my decision. I understood his reluctance. It was uncharted territory for us. In truth, it was a gamble, but one that I was willing to take, for the people, for our country.

"We can figure it out, Matt," I reassured him. "We'll hire the best thinkers, strategists. We'll run a grassroots campaign to involve the people directly. We’ll do this differently, better. I trust in the wisdom and power of our voters."

I watched as his hesitance melted away, replaced by a fiery determination. I knew then that I had, yet again, made the right choice. Matt was more than a campaign manager – he was a believer.

"All right, then," he murmured. His eyes sparkled with a resolve I hadn’t seen before and I allowed myself a small, entertained smirk. “Bring on the impossible.”

In saying that, he pushed open the door to a new path, a path devoid of shortcuts, easy wins, or political safety nets. It was a path of truth, wilderness, and perhaps, in the end, unexpected victory. After all, it had always been the 'impossible' that led to the greatest of revolutions, and maybe, it was our turn now.

That's because we tend to take them for granted. Trees have always been there. We grow up with them around us. We use their wood to build houses, their fruits to feed us and their leaves to provide shelter. However, we often forget the immense benefits they bring to our life and world. 

Trees serve as the earth's lungs, absorbing carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen into the atmosphere. Hence, they play a crucial role in limiting climate change. Moreover, they conserve water by producing shade, prevent soil erosion, and provide habitats for several species.

In cities, trees can significantly reduce pollution levels, decrease the heat during summer, and act as a noise barrier. Moreover, the presence of urban trees can improve our mental health. 

Despite these numerous advantages, deforestation and urbanization continue to significantly reduce the world's tree populations. More and more people live in environments where trees are sparse. This disconnection may be why many folks may jokingly question the existence of trees.

Nonetheless, there is growing awareness of the crucial role trees play in preserving life as we know it. Numerous initiatives worldwide aim to stop deforestation and encourage reforestation. Global movements, such as the Trillion Tree Campaign, hope to plant trees on a massive scale to combat climate change.

While trees might not play an active role in our daily thoughts or decisions, they undoubtedly contribute significantly to our quality of life. So, the next time you step outside, take a moment to appreciate the trees around you. Their quiet, steadfast presence is more than just background scenery; it's a lifeline.

Dear Dad,

I miss you more than words can say. I miss our long talks about life, our shared laughter during family dinners, and your warm hug that somehow always managed to make everything seem okay. 

Days turn into weeks and weeks into months, but the pain of your absence never seem to lessen. Every sunrise and sunset feel incomplete without you. Your wise words and caring voice still echo in my ears. 

I miss our Saturday morning fishing trips. The sparkle in your eyes when you caught a fish is something that I will remember for the rest of my life. And, how can I forget the hours spent in the garage tinkering with tools, fixing cars, and those thousands of life lessons learned from you?

I often find myself lost in captured moments, flipping through the pages of old photo albums, or just sitting silently in your favorite armchair. It is in these small things that I feel so close to you; like you’re still with me, guiding me like my North Star just like you always did.

The world looks different without you in it, Dad. The colors are less bright, the music less sweet. There is a certain tranquillity that seemed to have left with you. Missing you hurts, but it also reminds me of the precious times we had together, the love we shared, which no amount of time and space can take away.

Your love for Mom, for us, was so pure and undying. You taught us, by your example, how to live with dignity and grace, how to fight battles, how to love, how to forgive, and most importantly, how to be a family. Your life lessons are the greatest inheritance left for us – richer than any material wealth.

I kept replaying the last time we spoke, your calm voice and reassuring words – ‘everything will be okay.’ It was less of a good-bye and more of a ‘see you later.’ I didn’t know then, that it meant seeing you in my dreams and thoughts.

I know I have to continue without you by my side, but a part of you will always live within me. I find solace in the fact that heaven needed you more, that you are at a better place.

So here I am, Dad, doing my best as you taught me. Trying to find strength in my weaknesses, courage in my fears, and beauty in my breaks – just like you would have wanted me to. And above all, finding the will to continue and become a person you would be proud of.

As I end this letter, the tears may flow but so do the memories. I love you, I miss you and I’ll forever continue cherishing the love and lessons you left behind.

Till we meet again,
[Your Name]
