It was a tough feeling – I looked around my room, filled with toys, comics, a world map that I had hung on the wall, all seeming unfamiliar and out of place.

Imagine waking up one morning to find that you have aged by 65 years. That is precisely what had happened to me. I was eight- or at least I looked eight. But my mind had advanced, reached the ripening age of 73, and came bundled with memories of a life I had not even lived yet. It was a mixed bag of astounding intelligence, decades of experiences I couldn't remember living, skills I doubt my little body could carry out and not to mention the emotional maturity of a septuagenarian.

Now, life, as they say, must go on. And so, I decided to face the situation head-on. There were ethical, societal, emotional, physical, and academic challenges I had to consider, being a child with an adult brain.

Learning to manage these unparalleled circumstances was challenging. My parents and teachers didn't understand why I suddenly started discussing quantum mechanics and the global economic scenario. On the other hand, my physical body, being that of an eight-year-old, made it difficult for me to engage in adult conversations or to be taken seriously.

But as weeks turned into months, I viewed my situation not as a problem, but as an opportunity. I realized I was in a unique position to bring a new perspective to any topic. Whether it was schooling, family dynamics, or even video games - I approached all things differently.

I started to use my advanced understanding and experience in school, not only to excel acadically but also to help my peers. I started helping my dad with finances and even gave some useful retirement advice to my grandfather. I became the voice of reason in family quarrels and was able to bring a unique perspective to any situation.

It wasn't easy, but I figured out ways to navigate life with all its intricacies. I continued to grow and learn, despite my circumstances, and always strived to use my situation for the better.

So you see, age might define your experiences and learning, but it cannot restrict you if your determination and open-mindedness are steadfast. Life can throw you curveballs wrapped up as gifts, as it did to me. It all depends on how you unwrap that package and use what's inside of it.

For weeks now he had been surviving solely on whatever scraps he could find, mysterious greens and wild berries that did little but keep him from starving. He journeyed towards a distant town with the hope of finding something substantial to eat. The drawback, however, the town was infested with the undead – ruthless, ageless, night-shrouded creatures that clung to their half-life with a deadly desperation.

As he neared the town, the air turned frigid, and the sweet, sour smell of decay seemed to swallow him whole. He took a deep breath and began to muster the courage to move forward. He clasped a fist around the hilt of his weather-beaten sword; its blade still gleamed despite countless encounters with the undead.

With each step he fought away the fear welling inside of him. He reminded himself of his hunger, of the torment, of the stomach cramps that had become as steady as a heartbeat. He used that pain as a clarion call, driving him into the darkened town.

The moon cast an eerie glow, illuminating the decrepit buildings huddled close together like ancient comrades in fear, crumbling in the face of an eternal enemy. Stalk rack-thin figures in tattered rags shuffled along, shadows against the darkness. James clutched his sword even tighter. The undead were not his first choice of company, but circumstances had forced him into their territory.

The rotten smell grew more potent and struck his senses with all the subtlety of a sledgehammer. James grimaced and tried to quiet the instinct screaming inside him to get out. He recalled a chant he had learnt, a mantra to ward off the fear, as he creeped through the town's decaying streets.

His heart pounded so loudly he was sure the undead could hear its pulsating rhythm. And then he saw it. A small grocery store barely standing, its windows long shattered, and the grim facade covered with moss and decay. But perhaps it still harboured what James was searching for, something edible.

With a deep breath, he tightened his hold on his sword and advanced on the store. The chilling eyes of the undead followed his movement as he broke into a sudden sprint, defiance radiating from his every step.

Skin and bones they were. He could destroy them if it came down to it. But he would rather not, he reminded himself, he was here for food, not a fight.

Narrowly skirting past an undead, he burst into the grocery store. His eyes darted frantically, scanning for whatever he could find. Bread, fruits, snacks, anything. Anxiously, he rifled through the rubble. His rumbling belly spurred him on, moving the rotten debris aside. Suddenly, his hand met with something solid, a can of food.

A surge of relief passed through him, gripping the can tightly in his hands. He swiftly moved towards the exit, keeping a cautious eye on the restless undead. They seemed to have sensed his victory and their ravenous eyes followed him, their rotting fingers reaching out towards him.

But James was swift, his hunger fuelling his speed and determination, as he made his escape from the forsaken town. As he ran away into the silvery night, clutching the can of food, his heart-beating in triumph, he knew he had made it. His desperate search for food had defied the undead. Yes, James hated the undead, but he hated being hungry more.

As I sit down at the worn-out desk in my tiny apartment early in the morning, the calm silent atmosphere is still a stark contrast to the whirlwind of the past few days. The chaos started last Monday, when I was abruptly fired from my job at a prestigious law firm. The reasons for my dismissal were as vague as the firm’s high-minded ideals. Still reeling from the shock, I found myself in a coffee shop around the corner, drowning my sorrows in a cup of strong Americano and polishing off a blueberry muffin.

In the middle of my pitiful self-pity buffet, I was surprised by an old college buddy who suddenly popped up out of nowhere. Even more surprising was that he came not to offer consolation, but a business proposition. He had just moved back to town after a lucrative stint at Silicon Valley and started a tech firm - now he needed a lawyer to handle their legal matters.

After a quick tour of their office - which was far more open, lively and interesting than my old firm could ever be - I found myself agreeing to his terms, my intrigue sparked by the uniqueness of their invention.

Even though the working environment was significantly different, complete with Foosball tables, indoor plants, and beanbag chairs – the workload was just as heavy, if not more so. Each day was a sprint, reviewing patents, meeting potential investors, and familiarizing myself with technologies far beyond my comprehension.

So with the whirlwind week behind me, I find myself needing a brief respite. Today is going to be a slow day, a way to calm my nerves and align my thoughts again. Firmly, I make up my mind to not touch any legal documents at all, and instead decide to indulge myself in a book that had been collecting dust on my shelf for too long - "Sapiens", Yuval Noah Harari's history of humankind. Might as well dive into another kind of whirlwind - the one of human evolution.

I start reading, accompanied by the continuous low hum of the aging refrigerator and the occasional honk from the outside street. The day further solidifies its quiet presence with a soft patter of rain against the window. It becomes the melody that underscores my moment of tranquility after my chaotic week.

The echo of past hardships starts to lose its grip on me, and with a sense of personal satisfaction, I delve deeper into the book. The past week indeed had its ups and downs but it's part of progress. Today, though, is indeed the day things have finally settled down. And for now, I want nothing more than this pause, this peaceful silence, before I plunge back into the exciting storm tomorrow.

Groaning like a bear coming out of hibernation, he fumbled blindly with his cellphone. The blaring techno beat of his default alarm echoed in his throbbing head, a relic from his college days. Finally, after smacking the screen a few times, he managed to hit the right button and silence filled the room.

The relief was immediate but short-lived. Now the nauseating reminder of last night's escapades—that unique funk of stale beer, cold pizza, and regret—was free to assert itself into his senses. Now that the alcohol-induced haze was fading, Mark was painfully aware of his surroundings.

Around him, his normally tidy apartment was a battlefield of discarded containers and food scraps. His flatmates were strewn about on various pieces of furniture, in various stages of undress, and in various levels of consciousness. They'd really outdone themselves this time, he thought bitterly. 

Shaking his head, Mark gingerly kicked a couple of empty bottles out of the way as he padded into the kitchen. The bright, fluorescent light was harsh against his hangover, making him wince. Rifling through the cupboards, he searched for the hidden stash of aspirin he kept for times like these. 

Finding the white savior, he dry swallowed a couple and refilled his water glass. Drinking in huge gulps, he stared out the soot-smeared kitchen window, watching as the early morning light glimmered off dew-laden grass.

Mark was in his late twenties and working at a well-paid job in the city. Looking around at the mess in his apartment and the throbbing headache coursing through his skull, he couldn't shake the feeling that he was trapped in a life phase he should have outgrown by now. It was like Groundhog Day - the same parties, the same hangovers, and the same existential dread, echoing in perfect harmony.

But for now, he thought, concentrating on the soothing coolness of the water he was sipping, that was a problem for Future-Mark. Present-Mark had a hangover to nurse and a mess to clean. With another heavy sigh, he started the arduous task of picking up beer cans, one by one.

The old captain cursed, his skin as old as the creased maps he held for too long, the edges of the crumbled parchment were sharp enough to leave a trail of red dots on his wrinkled skin. Every single scrap of paper, each corner of map, and parchment containing cryptic riddles seemed to have waged a war against his aged, weather-hardened skin. 

He’d sailed every sea and braved the wave's wrath, wrestled with the eerie silence of the Sargasso and deciphered the whispers of the North Wind. He was a man of monumental resilience, yet these seemingly insignificant injuries became the bane of his existence. He was, after all, a mariner of the ocean vast and not the papery realms. 

Marks were visible everywhere, between his knobbly joints, under the tattered nails, poking corns of his weather-beaten feet. A scratch ran along the line of his bumpy nose, ending at the very summit of the tip. A side-splittingly peculiar spectacle for any onlooker.  

One could merely speculate how the Cutlass Captain got a paper cut on his tongue. Was he testing these riddles for their taste? Or was his stubby pipe not around, so he chose to chew on these cryptic sheets? Well, the truth remained as buried as the shipwrecks in his tales. 

Yet, amidst this petty adversity, he was still the now bedridden captain. He considered every wound and each sharp winces they brought as the paper's ploy to contain him. But, despite their attempts, the paper sentences couldn’t stop him instead, they spurred him on. With fiery determination, he dove into the sea of words, cryptic scripts and numbers, for they hid the key to his one last adventure. 

For the captain, these cuts were nothing but temporary inconveniences, small prices you pay for hunting the elusive treasure, perhaps the 'X' on these old, crumpled maps. His heart was a treasure chest full of untold stories—the story of these paper cuts was one more entry into that chest.

His cloak billowed around him, speckled with the same pallid light that sequins the relentless dark. Over a back hunched by time, the fabric hung like a wraith, shifting and dancing in the ghostly moonlight. His long beard was silver with age, wild, untamed and dusted with frost, it streamed down like a waterfall, cascading over the satin fabric of his attire.

His eyes, dulled with a thousand stories of pain, loss and ageless wisdom, reflected the inky midnight sky. They spoke of countless tales of adventures that no mortal could dare to tread. His visage masked with an impenetrable solemnity that came from eons of solitary existence, making his aura as profound as the universe's secrets themselves.

He walked slowly, each step an echo that reverberated through the silent night. His cane, gnarled and old as he was, clicked with an aged rhythm on the cobblestones under the twinkling sky. It was as if the moon and stars held their breath each time he stepped, so as not to disturb the potent yet poignant harmony.

His gnarled hands, trembling slightly, clutched an ancient, though potent, staff. Strange symbols, older than any written language that survives to this day, were carved into the dark wood. Mysterious energy seemed to pulse from it, an energy that only he could harness. Or perhaps, it was only he who dared to wield such power. 

The midnight air turned colder; he mumbled a spell, his voice a hoarse whisper welcome among the hush of the night. A faint shimmer of ethereal light encased him instantly, warming the frigid air around him. Showing the wizard’s unspoken connection with the mystical elements of life, something he had honed over centuries of practice, patience, and devotion.

The dark field on which he now stood was nothing more than an expanse of frost-hugged grass, appearing spectral under the lunar illumination. He was here on a mission; he was seeking someone or something, a being not of this realm, one that threatened the balance of his world.

This was not his first challenge, nor he feared, it would be his last. But this was the path he had chosen, or rather the path that had chosen him. As a guardian of realms, as a weaver of time, as a sage, a seer, a soldier, and a sorcerer. Till his last breath, he would strive to yield the staff, guide the magic, and protect the world he called home from threats known and unknown.

For he was not just a man, he was the last of the wizards, the last remaining thread in a tapestry woven by an ancient race of seers and sorcerers. He was the wise man of the eternal night, the one who guarded the realms from the precipice of chaos, the one who lurked in the shadows so that humanity could bask in the light. His was a burden heavier than the mountains and vaster than the sea. But amidst the desolation and the solitude, he carried on, always moving, always guarding, for he was the unsung hero of his realm.

"Indeed, it is my duty to lay any unrest to rest," I reply, my gaze drifting over the court. The lords and ladies are the true power players in my kingdom, each one with a web of informers and free to spin their own version of the truth until reality is cloaked in half-truths and nimbly dodged lies. "Contrary to what has been said by rumor mongers, we are not at war with our neighbouring realm."

An incredulous murmur ripples through the crowd instantly. Their shocked faces suggest that I might as well have just declared the sky is red. 

I raise my hands, calling for silence. "This is not to say we're suddenly in league with them either. No, our relationship remains much the same. Our forces have exchanged blows at the border. We've lost men and so have they," I state, the hard truth causing a silence to devour the murmur.

"Yes, there are conflicts, and yes, these are challenging times. But do not mistake a few border skirmishes as a declaration of war." I pause, my eyes scanning the crowd. "This unrest is caused by fear. Fear leads to chaos. And chaos," I point at them, "chaos benefits none of us. Order and unity, these are what we need in such times."

A thin veil of silence drapes over the room. I hope my words have resonated with them. It is time to stop these rumors that are sowing discord in our realm. As the king, it's up to me to hold things together. I pray I've done my part today. "Remember, we are stronger together. Do your part to spread truth, not fear."

A cheer goes up from the crowd, echoing through the room. I've given them something to cling to in troubled times. As they disperse, I can only hope that my words reach far and wide, dispelling the destructive rumors that are threatening to fracture my kingdom.

Every night, as I walked home from work, I would pass the old man sitting on a faded blue bench in the park. He was like a fixture – an integral part of the landscape. His name was George, although he was mostly known as ‘Old George’ due to his advancing years and somewhat gnarled appearance. But there was a certain charm about him, a particular sparkle in his grey-blue eyes that spoke volumes about the life he had led.

Every evening, without fail, I would find him in the same spot, hunched over a wood-carved chessboard. The pieces, worn and chipped due to years of use, would be meticulously arranged, ready for an enigmatic competitor. His hands, wrinkled and quaking slightly from years of toil and hardship, would move his pieces with utmost care and precision.

Sometimes, he played against some passersby, and other times, an unseen and anticipated opponent that could only be his lively imagination. An empty chair sat across him, its vacancy almost echoing a quiet invitation to any passerby. "Care to play a game?" the empty chair seemed to silently ask.

George frequently spoke about his younger days - his days as a Princeton graduate, his passion for mathematics, his stint in Navy during the war, his years as a prolific chess player, and his lovely wife, Andrea, who had passed away many years before. Each tale was rich, steeped in layers of wisdom and sentimentality.

His love for the game of chess never withered. Instead, it seemed to flourish with each passing day. He claimed it kept his mind sharp, his spirit robust. When asked if he ever grew tired of it, his response was the same. "Chess is like life, kid," he would say with a wise smile, "unpredictable, challenging, and requires lots of strategizing. Also, it's full of surprises. Each day brings a new game, a new challenge, just like life."

Despite his age and solitude, George never seemed lonely. He had his chess game and the ever-changing, yet ever the same park, which became his home ground. He brought a sense of continuity in a world that was spinning too fast, a sense of an unwavering faith in a world that was constantly evolving.

My evening walks home somehow always felt richer after encountering George. His tales, his wisdom, his passion for the game, all left me with a feeling of enduring hope. In him, it was always the same game, but yet somehow, it was different each day.

Shadows played on its green surface, swirled around by the dim overhead lights that cast a foreboding glow. The room was silent, the stale scent of cigar smoke lingering in the air, a relic from past games, past bids, past laughs, and past desperation.

The young man, long fingers traced the black outlines of the spades, diamonds, hearts, and clubs printed onto the felt, trying to draw courage from every fiber. There were years of stories etched into this table.

His heart pounded heavily, adrenaline coursing through his veins, amplifying the tension that had fallen upon the room. As though sensing his fear, the door creaked open, filling the room with a chilling breeze that swept away the thick smoky air and rustled through the discarded playing cards, enticing them into a haunting dance.

In walked Frank “The King” O'Sullivan; a silver-haired fox with steely eyes that glimmered under the dull lights, making him look much more sinister. Frank was a legend in this game, his name whispered fearfully and adoringly in the same breath. The King carried an aura of casual menace, his every step echoing his authority.

The room fell into a deeper silence. His reputation preceded him: ruthless, unpredictable, and with a killer poker face that could make the most seasoned players crumble. Tonight, he was the enemy. Tonight, the young man had to beat him, to prove himself in this underworld of high stakes poker.

As Frank approached the table, he pulled a worn-out deck from his pocket, his fingers dancing over the cards like a pianist, delicately, yet assertively. Everyone watched with bated breath as he dealt the hand, striking the felt and slicing through the tense quietude. 

The young man looked at his cards, two aces smiled back at him. He exchanged a quick, unnoticed glance with them, a reassurance he needed to put his game face on. The felt table had seen thousands of games, victories, and defeats. Tonight, he hoped it bore witness to his triumph over “The King”. 

And so, the game began. The faint lights danced off the polished surface of the chips. Their clinking noise slicing through the silence. The tale of David and Goliath was underway once more, the green felt table serving as their endless battlefield.

This unique power of mine, it did not come with an instruction manual. No one was there to hold my trembling hand when I first time-jumped. Somehow, the clock and I were together, intertwined in an unusual dance. A reality hidden from the world, a truth that only I knew. Walking through timelines, tasting the past and the future, and yet standing firmly in the present hauling back to the reality. 

I touched a worn photo, feeling the raised edges and creases that bore testaments to its age. There was Grandma in her youthful bloom – a face parallel to mine. But this was back when our family was still an idea - a mere flutter in her heart. Closing my eyes and reaching a deep fragment within me, a pull echoed through my mind, and then, the world changed.

With a dizzying rush, blurred images swirled around me; a collage of time - of then, now, and beyond - and suddenly, I was standing amidst a bustling marketplace, under a sign reading: "Yorkshire, 1936." Grandma's year, her world. Now, my reality. My heart fluttered in the thrill of history unfolding itself.

Time manipulation, a misnomer. I was not its master; it was a feral creature, a vast ocean that threatened to wash over me. I traveled through it, yes, but the control was an illusion. Time was no straight line but an infinite number of threads entwining and splintering. And picking up those threads required strength, courage, and a touch of madness.

My encounters with the past were often enlightening, yet they carried a burden. There was so much I could change, so much pain I could prevent, but that came at a dangerous price. There's a rich tapestry of human history that weaves us together, and every thread I changed risked unraveling another. So, however torturous, I lived with the knowledge and did nothing.

And God, the future was even more intoxicating; the allure of knowing the unknown. But the mosaic of future visions were tantalizingly incomplete and wildly uncertain since the future was a tapestry still being woven - prickly and malleable.

In the absolute silence of my room, the pendulum tick-tocking relentlessly, I began to understand the magnitude of my power. A paradox in itself, bestowed upon a mere human, who was nothing more than a speck within the grandeur of cosmos. With the cosmos under my fingertips, the threads of time weaving patterns around me, I braced myself to face what lay ahead.

And so, I venture on, a silent guardian of time, keeping its secrets, reveling in its mysteries, and respecting its power. For, if Nothing is written in stone, then Time is etched in water, ebbing and flowing with the cosmic tide, and I was the carrier of its ebb and flow, a wave master in the river of time. I am more than just a Time Traveler; I am the Time weaver, Time dweller, the Timewalker.

"To be original is the ultimate challenge," my mentor often said, but I detested that line. The notion of originality made it seem like everything great had already been done, and this left no room for those of us struggling to make our mark on the world. His words began to chip away at my enthusiasm. When cerebral sparks for what I believed were revolutionary ideas ignited in my mind, they were immediately extinguished by that infamous phrase.

"It's been done before," he would state bluntly, a dismissive wave of his hand rendering my ideas worthless. It became a mantra that echoed in my ears, seeping deeply into my psyche. It critically undermined my confidence, my passion began to flail, every creative nerve begging for mercy.

The words became a beast I wrestled with every day. It grew, feeding off my insecurity, snarling at my attempts to appease it with innovative ideas. I fell victim to the discouragement, productivity strangled by a shadow of self-doubt. The passion that once coursed through me with vigor was now the feeble flicker of a single candle struggling against a tempest.

One evening, while marinated in frustration, I decided to take a different approach. If everything had been done before, it was time to stop trying to be entirely original and instead lend a new perspective to the existing world, to the already done. I set out to improve, innovate, and redefine.

And so, I began to experiment, stripping away everything I had learned, breaking down concepts, techniques, and ideas into their most basic forms. I examined them with a fresh pair of eyes, unfettered by prejudice or preconceptions. Refusing to be limited by what was 'done,' I embarked on a journey of exploration, of curiosity, and ultimately, of self-realization.

I discovered that there was beauty in reshaping the conventional, in challenging the usual, as long as it was backed with intention and meaning. The obsession with uniqueness, I realized, was a trap. Instead, it was the pursuit of understanding and meaningful creation that held true value.

Armed with this new-found conviction, I emerged from the shadows of the beast. My creations, while not entirely new in the most literal sense, carried the indelible stamp of my perspectives and the depth of my understanding.

Now, when I hear the phrase, "It's been done before," all it brings out of me is a healthy chuckle, laden with the wisdom of my previous struggles. It's a friendly reminder of the transformation in my ethos—a journey from despair to self-assuredness. Please, let those words come; they now harbor no fear but only fuel the fire of my individuality. The beast within had been tamed, and it was now a wellspring of inspiration. Yes, it's indeed been done before, but never my way.

In the end, it was not about being original, but about being authentic. It was about pouring heart and soul into my work, making it unabashedly mine and adding value in my unique way. I stop striving for originality and start embodying my authenticity, creating a beautiful amalgamation of the old and new with a flair distinctly mine, distinctly unique.

After Famine, their sights were set on Pestilence. The town had been prepared for this. After the long, grueling fight against Famine which had stripped them of their livelihood, they were already living a life of strict hygiene, rationing, and relentless farm work. The community built, repaired, and worked tirelessly to secure the town against Pestilence's plagues. 

Pestilence, much like Famine, didn't seem all that intimidating at first. He was an old, haggard man with a fragile body that would falter with a strong gust of wind. Yet when he did arrive at the town, his emaciated, sallow form concealed a deadly potency. As soon as he came, the first people fell. 

Still, they fought, armed with herbs, sanitization, and their most vital weapon – determination. It felt like nature was hell-bent on wiping them out, a weak colony of humans in a desolate wasteland. But they stood their ground, tending to one another, banding together like a close-knit family.

They fell, one by one, adding to the growing pile of bodies against which they waged their war. Pestilence’s hideous laugh echoed through the air, signaling another soul claimed. 

But the townsfolk didn't fall apart. A compassion, unity, and determination spread through them, more infectious than the plague Pestilence brought. They managed to isolate the sick, treated them with tried and tested herbal remedies, and burnt the bodies – an act of respect for the fallen and a strategic move against spreading the infection. 

Eventually, their ceaseless trials paid off. With every lost member, their resolve hardened, and soon the echoes of Pestilence’s laughter dwindled. The weak and frail man succumbed to the very plague he'd intended for them.

With Pestilence vanquished, they were left with two more Horsemen– War and Death. The colony was already reeling from the blows of Famine and Pestilence. Dealing with War and Death seemed insurmountable, a daunting challenge almost beyond their reach. Yet, they'd come this far, survived the unfathomable. They couldn't falter now. It was time to prepare again, to rally their defenses and brace themselves for confronting the last two Horsemen.

His voice was unnaturally soothing, completely contradicting his menacing appearance. His fiery eyes glowed in the quaint, dimly lit room. The walls of the expansive chamber, adorned with ancient murals lent an aura of surrealism to the scene. 

"Thank you...I suppose," I muttered which was all my surprise would allow me to say. Rules of manners seem to hold even when you're interacting with entities from different dimensions.

"It's not often I receive human guests," the demonic entity rumbled, its voice resonating off the stone walls around us, "It's an honor to host a being with such resilience and unique spirit."

"I don't suppose you often invite them," I shot back, surprising myself. It seems I had left the realm of fear and was entering the surreal domain of sarcasm. I decided to embrace this strange turn of my usual ironical humor, who knows, it might be my last chance to be quirky again.

The demon let out a deep hearty laugh that echoed ominously throughout the room. "Ah, you humans," he said, grinning revealing an array of sharp white teeth, "I can see why you are favored by some above."

Otherworldly trinkets and artifacts adorned the shelves around the room, creating a stark contrast to the simple but oddly comforting wooden furniture. The lurking sense of danger made the scene unbearably eerie. 

"So, what's the purpose of my summoning?" I managed to ask, somehow maintaining my composure. My mind had veered off to wonder how the hell I got caught in this in the first place. One moment, I was doodling weird symbols from a book I'd found in a thrift store, next I was standing in the apparently cozy living room of the devil himself.

The demon arched one of its thick, fiery eyebrows. "Summoning?" he echoed, "Oh no, John. I didn't summon you. The markings you traced out...that was an invitation issued by you."

"Oh look at that," I muttered to myself. Note to self - avoid doodling symbols from ancient books, you don't know when it may end up being an invite to a demon's living room. The demon continued eyeing me expectantly, seemingly unfazed by my continued sarcastic remarks. Maybe it was used to human theatrics, or maybe it needed some entertainment, after all, the underworld did seem a bit dull.

I took a deep breath, steadying myself, before announcing, "Well, I'm here now. Might as well make the most of it. What's the plan then, a tour of hell or a tea party?"

The demon laughed again, "Your kind never ceases to amaze me." He motioned for me to sit, "Let's start with the tea, shall we? And perhaps we could discuss...deal of sorts. It's not every century I get a mortal in my realm." 

Tea with the devil? A deal? I had a million questions running through my mind. But my dry throat could do with some tea. So, I decided to sit, sip, listen, and humor the devil...for now. An unexpected adventure was at hand, and I was ready to step up to the plate as the reluctant hero. 

After all, an ordinary man's tale might not capture the interest of many, but a story about enduring a supernatural evening with a demon just might.

Underneath the jealous watch of an iron-fisted sky, the unhallowed ground quakes in utter dread of his coming. To the villagers, this merry hamlet named Bethlehem is a place of tranquility and refuge, but for the one they call 'Shaitan', it is a battlefield where the lines between good and evil blur.

He revels in the simmering chaos, the irreversible plunge into darkness. Those whose eyes have witnessed this dread demon now bear etchings of despair and helplessness within their souls. The shadows cast by the moonless sky do little to hide his monstrous form. There is no deceit, no subterfuge - Shaitan is the embodiment of unabated terror and annihilation.

Fleshing out from the swirling winds and suffocating dust, the beast that once only existed within nightmares now stands bare, tangible and devastatingly intimidating. The hardened sinew of his musculature coils over his skeletal frame, in an intimidating display of supernatural strength and raw power. He breathes into the night, a primal and sinister hiss escaping his dreadful maw, his demonic eyes glinting crimson with malevolent intent. 

He watches with amusement as the villagers scramble to barricack their homes, the ominous clang of hammer against nail serving as the discordant symphony of their impending fate. They pray to their sacred deities for deliverance, yet they harbor a nauseous dread deep within their hearts. They have felt this terror before. They recognize it. Embrace it. Know it by name - Shaitan.

Yet a glimmer of rebellion kindles in the heart of Bethlehem, sparked by those who refuse to abandon their land and faith. They forge weapons from iron and from fear itself. If it was terror that the Lord of Hell wished to sow, then they would respond in kind. 

In the end, the Beast was not the only one born of shadows. Even a tiny hamlet has her protectors. Shaitan, in his devastating grandeur, may be a difficult mountain to overcome. But like the dust from which he was born, a gust of hope, of righteousness, can scatter him to the winds. 

Prepared they stand, at the precipice of a battle destined to stain the annals of Bethlehem history. Shaitan has come, but so have the guardians of humanity. 

Thus, under the unforgiving vastness of the starless heavens, began the epic confrontation between Shaitan and Bethlehem. A battle for dominion, a battle for existence, a battle that would choose either light or perpetual darkness — the survival of humanity hanging precariously in the balance.

I frequently replay the night in my mind, that fateful argument wherein words left my mouth quicker than thoughts formed. I pray for a chance to tell you now, that those harsh words were not the truth, rather my stubborn ego that desperately wanted to win the fight.

I recall your beautiful face filled with hurt which I never intended to inflict, your hazel eyes glistening with fallen tears that I wished I could have stopped. The worst part was the sight of you walking away, your figure disappearing through that door which, in agony, I impulsively slammed shut.

I have spent countless nights, alone, wishing for that moment to reoccur, if only to change the outcome. I would apologize, say the things I should have said, admit my wrongs and my insecurities, and voice out the feelings I held back.

Often, I reminisce about our days together; our laughter, small tiffs, shared secrets, and the promise of a future. And it hits me every time, the vacuum in my life that your absence has left. My daily routine feels mundane without your enchanting presence, coffee tastes bitter without your sweet words, the rising sun seems dull without your smile, and the beauty of the twilight seems worthless without you by my side.

The silence in our once shared apartment screams about the emptiness, and every corner still whispers your name. How can I not miss you, Marissa, when every single thing around me sings about you?

I yearn for the comfort of your voice, for the reassurance of your touch, and the love in your gaze. My heart craves for you, the way a parched desert longs for the first rain.

It took me losing you to realize my foolishness, to understand the depth of my love for you, and how I took your love for granted. Regret, they say, comes last, and it seems truer now than ever.

I am writing this not to burden you with my feelings but to release the heaviness off my chest, with a hope that someday, you will understand why I did what I did, and maybe, just maybe, forgive me.

With not much to offer than a heavy heart filled with remorse and boundless love for you, I fervently hope that we could start afresh.

Ever since you have walked out of that door, a part of me walked out with you - perhaps the best part of me.

The dilapidated tea set had been my grandmother's, a token of a forgotten era where the porcelain was worn thin with age, the deep colors faded awash with the unrelenting passage of time, and the lustrous gold that once lavishly adorned it was now simply dull with a patina hinting at past grandeur. They were bundled up in layers of dusty old newspapers, tucked away in the shadows of a rickety, old wooden cupboard. The cups were chipped and cracked from years of use, and the teapot handle was weak, threatening to break with every touch. 

The teacups danced clumsily around whenever I tried to line them up, their bottoms uneven, warped by the pressure of the years they bore. The once intricately designed spoons had been used so often that the patterns were hardly recognizable, replaced by scrapes and scratches that told tales of countless afternoon teas. The sugar pot was the only survivor, having retained some semblance of durability with just a hint of its delicate, flowery pattern still visible. 

Each and every time the set was used, I heard my grandmother's voice echoing in my ears, reminding me of the countless stories spilled over cups of her ginger-infused tea. Despite the extent of the decay, I remember the gleam in her eyes as she cradled the teapot in her hands, pouring tea with a deliberate delicacy that I've never been able to replicate. 

In the end, it was not just a tea set. It was a memory, a remnant of a grand past now long gone, that connected me to a history, a heritage. Each crack and chip, each stain and scratch, told stories of bygone eras filled with joy, laughter, sorrow and wisdom.  

Yet, they also signaled the impending demise of this ancient relic. Despite my best efforts at preservation, the set seemed to crumble a little more with every use, the cracks forming a web, creeping their way across the faded porcelain with a cruel inevitability. The old set, like a grand and ancient building, was marked for demolition, not due to some sudden catastrophe, but from the slow, insidious wear of unrelenting time.

One day, very soon, I knew I would reach for them and find only fragments. And with their death would come the end of an era. An era framed by priceless memories, drenched in the aroma of my grandmother's ginger tea, and bound by conversations that transcended generations. But until that day, the tea set would still hold a cup of warm memories, some faded laughter, and aged well-wishes.

The stark black expanse, dotted with twinkling stars, enveloped him with both soothing tranquility and a haunting sense of the unknown. He had spent countless evenings like this one, lying on his back in the field outside his home, gazing upward, questions swimming in his head like school of perplexed fish. His mind spanned the distant galaxies, attempting to dissect and comprehend the grand mysteries of the universe. 

There was so much he didn't understand, yet he was drawn to it all the same. The infinite beauty, the silent symphony of celestial bodies far beyond his reach, whispered tales of endless possibilities, uncharted realms, and unseen marvels. Each star held a history, a story, blinking in codes waiting to be deciphered. His eyes fluttered from one bright light to another, trying to keep up with his racing thoughts.

The cool grass caressed his scattered hair, the tickling sensation grounding him back to Earth from his cosmic journey. A shooting star briefly etched its path across the night, capturing his awe and momentarily pushing away his worries. As a child, he had been told, they were celestial bodies bowing out after centuries of existence, granting a single wish to those fortunate enough to spot them. A soft smile crossed his face as he closed his eyes and let his heart whisper a silent wish.

For him, the sky held a promise, one that he had decided to commit his life to. It offered him direction, adventure, and a chance to be part of something greater. The vastness of the cosmos reminded him of how insignificant his problems were, compared to the grand scheme of things. All those nights spent under the starry blanket offered him solace and perspective, taking away some of his worldly burdens. 

For a moment, he lost himself in the dreams of what the future could hold. The anticipation knotted his stomach, but it was a good kind of nervousness. He would sail through the sea of stars, get lost in nebula clouds, and grapple with black holes. The universe's mysteries would be his exploration path. Standing at the top of the staircase, Brian caught the aroma of freshly brewed coffee mingling with the smell of baking pastries, a signature morning smell in their home.

As soon as he stepped foot into the room, his eyes fell on his wife standing in the kitchen. She was positioned in front of the stove, her hair up in a messy bun, a few loose strands hanging loosely by her ears. Dressed in her favorite baggy pyjamas, the sunlight streaming in from the window making her honey-brown highlights shine, she looked incredibly beautiful to him.

Susan, his wife's eyes darted up as she heard his footsteps and warmed at the sight of her husband awake. She went back to overviewing the pancakes on the stove as she greeted him. "Morning, sleepyhead. I didn't think you'd be up so soon," she said, her voice resonating with warmth and affection.

Brian chuckled at her words as he sauntered into the kitchen, his half-closed eyes making him squint as he adjusted to the brightness.

He admired his wife's tranquil demeanor as she perfectly flipped a pancake, and an amused smile played across his lips. Not everyone could look this elegant, this early, while cooking breakfast. He always admired her energy in the morning, her vigour was contagious.

Devouring the warm sight of his wife bustling around in the kitchen, Brian silently went to the beautifully aged mahogany table and slid into his usual seat. He had a custom to read a deductive mystery book in the morning, a habit provided by his crime novelist wife. Picking up the finely printed book, he tried hard to suppress his sleep-laden eyes as he allowed his wife's symphony of morning cooking to become the perfect background.

"Anything interesting?" she asked, with a curious tilt of her head, her hazel eyes glittering with interest.

"Nah, not really, it's hard to track down the criminal when one is half awake," he replied with a chucky grin, closing the book and pouring himself a cup of coffee.

Her laughter echoed in the kitchen, a sound Brian found himself eagerly looking forward to every morning. He knew this was not just an ordinary morning - it was another day in his blissful life.

Although shaken by the long period of unconsciousness, Gretchen was a fighter. She quickly familiarized herself with the critical technological and cultural changes that had taken place since 2016. This news filled her with hope and determination. She had strongly believed in his progressive agenda and felt that it had the potential to create a more equitable society, especially regarding issues close to her heart: women's rights and LGBTQ+ rights.

She deeply regretted not being able to vote in 2016, but that only made her more determined to get involved this time. She started by reaching out to her old political buddies and was welcomed back with open arms. They were thrilled to see her well and were struck by her unwavering commitment to her principles despite the years-long ordeal.

Gretchen immediately got involved in campaigning for Bernie Sanders again, leveraging the vast networks she had built over the years. Passionate and motivated, she travelled from town to town, speaking to voters and convincing them about Bernie's vision of tuition-free college education, medicare for all, and the importance of addressing income inequality.

Moreover, Gretchen also actively advocated for LGBTQ+ rights, women's rights, and socialism. She organized rallies, seminars, online campaigns and spoke at public forums to address these issues. She had always dreamed of an egalitarian society free from discrimination and the vast wealth gap, and she was not going to let her years of coma deter her from fighting for these causes.

Just as she had before her coma, Gretchen continued to inspire and lead, proving that no amount of time or hardship could dampen her unwavering spirit and commitment to her ideals.

"What is this... mirage, illusion?" He muttered under his breath, still focused on the impenetrable blackness before him. His heart banged against his ribcage, the rhythm frantic as a trapped bird. He rubbed his eyes with the heel of his hands and then looked again. Still there was this unnatural, baffling, vast nothingness that defied explanation.

"Ah, I see what you mean." I tried to control the confusion and slight embarrassment creeping into my voice. "Well, it's a he to me. Erebus is his name."

"You knocked on our familiar, homey wooden table." the detective looked nonplussed at best. "An eldritch being. Named Erebus."

"Yes."

"He's from another dimension."

"Yes."

"And you love him."

I gulped, looking at the detective's piercing gaze. Why are human feelings so hard to explain sometimes? Why is the idea of loving something beyond the physical so puzzling? I still managed to maintain some pride. "Yes, I love him."

An awkward silence filled the room, only the ticking of the old grandfather clock providing some semblance of a rhythm to our conversation. I imagined hearing the creaking of Erebus' interdimensional form, the low, comforting hum of his otherworldly presence—but it was only my hopeful imagination. The skepticism that radiated from the investigator only reminded me further of his absence.

The detective finally broke the silence after what seemed like an eternity. "Is he...er...safe?"

I hesitated. "For you, if you're asking about potential physical harm, I'd say yes. Erebus won't intentionally harm any humans."

"What about you?"

I could see the slight concern sneak into their gaze— it was a rarity to have an enquiry about me. "Physically, inherent damage doesn't exist when we're together. Mentally, on the other hand..." I let a soft, loving smile play on my lips as the waves of bittersweet emotions threatened to overwhelm me. "I'll never be the same, and I don't think I'd want to be."

He didn't seem to know what to make of it. I don't blame him. It's not every day you meet someone who loves an entity from another dimension. But I do, despite the improbability of it all. And I wouldn't trade it for anything else. 

Detective or not, he didn't need to understand. Not everyone can comprehend the cosmic connections of the universe, let alone the bond between a human and an eldritch being. As for the gender pronouns, well, love doesn't care about that either. 

His name is Erebus. He's from another dimension. And I love him. That's all that truly matters.

In modern usage, a scapegoat is an individual, group, or entity unjustly blamed for wrongs done by others. It is often a convenient target upon which to project blame rather than addressing the actual source of an issue. The concept comes from this ancient religious practice of transferring sins onto an innocent animal, or "scapegoat," to expiate wrongdoing.

The waiting room is a typical one; not very big, not very small either. Its beige walls are adorned with generic art posters; a kitten in a basket, a sunset over a sea, a picture of a laughing child. The seats lining the walls are upholstered in the same uninspiring color, exuding a strange sense of calm and boredom simultaneously. A small coffee table in the center is strewn with months-old magazines, the edges of the pages curling up slightly.

I look out the sizable window, watching as edited snippets of the world outside move by - office goers passing by in a hurry, children skipping along, a scruffy looking sparrow preening its feathers. The sky is a brilliant blue, almost blindingly so, dotted here and there by fluffy white clouds.

The clock on the wall ticks away, the sound so rhythmic and monotonous that it's almost hypnotic. The receptionist, a young woman, taps away on her keyboard, the staccato typing noise blending with the clock's ticking to create an unusual cadence.

Every now and then, she glances up at me and gives a reassuring smile, as if to say that my turn will come soon. But time seems to have a mind of its own here; it crawls at a snail's pace, unhurried and languid.

A man in a suit and tie walks in, looks around disapprovingly and sits down across from me. He takes out his phone and starts to swipe at the screen furiously, muttering under his breath. The minutes continue to crawl by as the room fills with more people, each lost in their own world.

Occasionally, a door off to the side opens, and a slender woman with a clipboard steps out. She reads a name out, and one lucky person is allowed to escape from the endless waiting game. As I wait for her to call my name, I lose myself again in the symphony of sounds and the monotonous world just beyond the window.

Upon his apprehension in June 2014, Mark Johnson was charged with the robbery of a gas station in Riverside, California. The prosecution claimed that Johnson had taken an undisclosed amount of money from the cash register and a variety of goods from the convenience store, all while threatening the cashier with what appeared to be a handgun.

After his arrest, Johnson strongly insisted that he was innocent. He claimed that he was a victim of mistaken identity and he was nowhere near the gas station at the time of the crime. Despite his plea, the case against Johnson seemed strong. Johnson matched the physical description of the suspect from the CCTV footage provided by the gas station, and he was identified by the cashier as the man who robbed the store. In addition, items reportedly stolen from the gas station were discovered in Johnson's car upon arrest.

Johnson's attorney immediately challenged the prosecution's claims, arguing about the legality of the search of Johnson's car and the reliability of the cashier's eyewitness account. Moreover, there were concerns about the quality of the CCTV footage and the subsequent identification of Johnson as the alleged perpetrator.

In the trial, Johnson's defense attorney questioned the arresting officer about the search of Johnson's vehicle, which he argued was carried out without a proper warrant and, therefore, any evidence obtained should be inadmissible.

On the other hand, the prosecution held that the search was legal due to the plain view doctrine which allows law enforcement officers to seize evidence and contraband found in plain view during a lawful observation. They also emphasized the cashier's confident identification of Johnson and the relevance of the stolen items found in his possession.

The jury, after several days of deliberation, returned with a guilty verdict. This decision was appealed by Johnson's lawyer citing that the judge should have suppressed the controversial evidence from Johnson's car.

Finally, the case was referred to the California Supreme Court in 2016. The high court was tasked to review the critical point of contention which was the legality of the search of Johnson's car. The court's decision was not only going to impact Johnson's fate but also has significant implications on law enforcement procedures in the state of California.
